region.text: Delhi city and the territory as far as Palam

events.note: Shah Alam II page: Mahadji Scindia took Delhi on 2 October 1788 and restored the emperor; 'Second reign: 16 October 1788 - 19 November 1806'; the emperor became a client of Scindia's Gwalior State, which kept a garrison in Delhi, and he was 'only left with Delhi city to rule'. Gwalior's ledger/4 (1788/10) gains the whole Delhi-Agra region from the Mughal Empire and takes the emperor's last cell, so the Mughal Empire vanished from the map from October 1788 although its second reign began on 16 October and lasted to 1806. The emperor's seat (Delhi city to Palam, the mughal-empire_1783 correction) goes back to the Mughal Empire, drawn as Gwalior's vassal by the relation Gwalior's ledger opens in 1784.

correction.text: the thirteen states plus the land west to the Mississippi and north of 31N: the Old Northwest, Kentucky, Tennessee, Georgia, Alabama and Mississippi, less the Natchez strip and the British forts; the disputed north of Maine (Aroostook and the upper Saint John valley) is left out until the Webster-Ashburton Treaty of 1842; plus the treaty land the correction had dropped: Minnesota east of the Mississippi (the Arrowhead and the upper river), the western edge of Wisconsin, the Kentucky holes and the southern strip of Georgia

keyframe_overrides.why: Treaty of Paris (1783), Article 2 as the page quotes it: the line runs through the Great Lakes to 'the northwesternmost point' of the Lake of the Woods, 'and from thence on a due west course to the river Mississippi', then 'along the middle of the said river' to 31 N; the page adds that the Mississippi 'does not extend that far northward', so that line never meets the river. So everything east of the Mississippi up to the Lake of the Woods line went to the United States. The keyframe's correction lists states inside a box of 92 W to 66 W and 31 N to 50 N and omits Minnesota, so the 399 Minnesota cells Quebec held (province-of-quebec_1774 polygon) were released to nobody in 1783 and then taken by the Spanish Empire's 'Louisiana' region in 1788; the box also cut 43 western Wisconsin cells and 33 southern Georgia cells, and Kentucky has 31 holes in Cliopatria's shape. Applies 1783-1787. [Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: the Minnesota polygon copied from province-of-quebec_1774 also took in about 110 cells west of the river (south-east Minnesota below Hastings, where the river is the Wisconsin line, and the Leech Lake pocket); it is now cut along the river. Against the current dossiers the Minnesota figures differ: Quebec held 111 Minnesota cells east of the river (released to nobody in 1783, taken by Spain in 1788), Spanish Louisiana 87 west of it and Rupert's Land 202 north of 47 N (p1770-p1779 rulings/2); R1 kept the Rupert's Land cells against this claim, so rulings/2 of this file gives the 180 of them east of the river to the United States.]

keyframe_overrides.why: Agha Mohammad Khan page: after Karim Khan's death he defeated his brothers, 'conquering Mazandaran' (2 April 1779). The Zand ledger already takes Mazandaran out in 1779, but the 1780 keyframe (Cliopatria's Karim Khan polygon) puts its 83 cells back for 1780-1787, so Mazandaran was drawn Zand until the 1788 shape dropped it. Removed from the 1780 shape; the land stays unowned until the Qajar founding of 1789 (Qajar dynasty ledger/0).

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier already removes the 30 stray Canadian cells of Cliopatria's 1788 East India Company shape ('held no Canadian land'); one more stray cell lies in the Minnesota Arrowhead (48.0 N, 90.2 W), drawn as a single speckle of the Company in the Boundary Waters from 1788. The East India Company page shows no North American holding in the 1780s: its link to North America is trade ('sell tea from its colonies in Asia in the American colonies'), and it 'gained control of large parts of the Indian subcontinent and Saint Helena'. Applies 1788-1790 (1790 is in the next window).

rulings.why: The Province of Quebec was its own colony: 'established by the Kingdom of Great Britain in 1763', enlarged by the Quebec Act of 1774 to the Labrador coast and the land south and west of the Great Lakes, and divided into Lower and Upper Canada only in 1791. The British Colonial Empire is Cliopatria's umbrella shape; by the colony rule (R1) the umbrella's smaller keyframe took 466 cells of Quebec's own land in 1780 (Quebec province 351, Ontario 53, Labrador 49, Michigan 11) and 490 in 1783 (Quebec 350, Ontario 56, Labrador 84). The colony keeps its land, as the p1770-p1779 patch ruled for 1775-1779. [Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: region added to leave out the Detroit-area cells in Michigan. Given to Quebec for 1780-1782, they were released to nobody in 1783 by Quebec's ledger/3 (the United States correction leaves Detroit out), so the ruling widened the Detroit hole of 1783-1787 from 7 to 12 cells; left to the umbrella, 5 of them stay British, as the page has it: 'the British maintained a military presence there until 1796'.]

region.text: every cell both claim except the Detroit area on the Michigan side
the 49-50.3 N band of north-western Ontario that Rupert's Land held up to 1782 (Lac Seul, the Lake Nipigon country and the Albany headwaters)

rulings.why: The Quebec Act set Quebec's northern boundary at 'the southern boundary of lands owned by the Hudson's Bay Company, or Rupert's Land'. The 1783 Quebec keyframe (Upper Canada region) overlaps the Rupert's Land keyframe over 266 cells of north-western Ontario between 49 N and 50 N, and R1 gave them to Quebec as the smaller colony; Rupert's Land held them before 1774 and through 1782 (p1770-p1779 rulings/2 ruled the same 266 cells for 1774-1779), and no page dates a change of the line in 1783, so Rupert's Land keeps them. [Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: the why had called the whole band Hudson Bay drainage, which no page opened says, and cited the earlier ruling for Minnesota only.]

rulings.why: Treaty of Paris (1783), Article 2 as the page gives it: the line runs through 'Lake Superior ... Long Lake, Lake of the Woods' to 'the northwesternmost point' of the Lake of the Woods 'in present-day Minnesota', 'and from thence on a due west course to the river Mississippi', then down the river; so northern Minnesota east of the Mississippi and south of that line went to the United States. Rupert's Land held 180 of these cells (north of 47 N, from the p1770-p1779 ruling against Quebec) and R1 kept them against the 1783 and 1788 US keyframes (keyframe_overrides/0-1). [Added by the reviewer, 2 Nov 2026.]
